difficulty_reason: The lemma records six implications: Noetherian implies adic*, adic* implies adic, adic implies weakly adic, weakly adic implies classical, weakly adic implies countably indexed, and countably indexed implies McQuillan (statement lines 2452-2467). The first four are obtained by writing the space as the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological ring and invoking the corresponding implications between the types of such rings, which are collected in a section of the chapter (proof lines 2469-2474). The fifth is proved from the definition: a weakly adic ring has a countable fundamental system of open ideals by definition, and the space is the colimit of the spectra of the quotients by those ideals, which presents it as countably indexed (proof lines 2476-2483). The sixth is proved by writing the space as a colimit of thickenings of affine schemes and observing that the ring of the limit surjects onto each of the rings of the stages, because the transition maps are surjections as the morphisms are closed immersions, which is exactly the condition for being McQuillan (proof lines 2485-2490). The claim is H2: the first four parts are transfers to a cited collection of ring-theoretic implications, but the last two are proved directly from the definitions, one by exhibiting a countable presentation and one by identifying a surjection onto each stage.
